zadanie:
Find all values of $k$ for which the system
\begin{align*}
x + ky - z &= 0, \\
kx - y - z &= 0, \\
x + y - kz &= 0
\end{align*}has a non-trivial solution.  (In other words, find all values of $k$ for which the system has a solution other than $(x,y,z) = (0,0,0).$)
oczekiwana_odpowiedz:
We can write the system as
\[\begin{pmatrix} 1 & k & -1 \\ k & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & -k \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}.\]This system has a nontrivial system exactly when the determinant of the matrix is 0.  This determinant is
\begin{align*}
\begin{pmatrix} 1 & k & -1 \\ k & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & -k \end{pmatrix} &= \begin{vmatrix} -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -k \end{vmatrix} - k \begin{vmatrix} k & -1 \\ 1 & -k \end{vmatrix} + (-1) \begin{vmatrix} k & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} \\
&= ((-1)(-k) - (-1)(1)) - k((k)(-k) - (-1)(1)) - ((k)(1) - (-1)(1)) \\
&= k^3 - k.
\end{align*}The solutions to $k^3 - k = k(k - 1)(k + 1) = 0$ are $\boxed{-1,0,1}.$

[AI]:
To determine the values of \( k \) for which the system of equations has a non-trivial solution, we can represent the system in matrix form and analyze the determinant of the coefficient matrix. The system can be written as:

\[
\begin{bmatrix}
1 & k & -1 \\
k & -1 & -1 \\
1 & 1 & -k
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}
x \\
y \\
z
\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
0 \\
0 \\
0
\end{bmatrix}
\]

A non-trivial solution exists if the determinant of the coefficient matrix is zero. We will calculate the determinant of the matrix:

\[
A = \begin{bmatrix}
1 & k & -1 \\
k & -1 & -1 \\
1 & 1 & -k
\end{bmatrix}
\]

We will compute the determinant using the formula for the determinant of a \( 3 \times 3 \) matrix:

\[
\text{det}(A) = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg)
\]

where the matrix is:

\[
\begin{bmatrix}
a & b & c \\
d & e & f \\
g & h & i
\end{bmatrix}
\]

For our matrix \( A \):

- \( a = 1, b = k, c = -1 \)
- \( d = k, e = -1, f = -1 \)
- \( g = 1, h = 1, i = -k \)

Now we can compute the determinant:

\[
\text{det}(A) = 1((-1)(-k) - (-1)(1)) - k(k(-k) - (-1)(1)) - 1(k(1) - (-1)(-1))
\]

Calculating each term:

1. First term:
   \[
   1(k + 1) = k + 1
   \]

2. Second term:
   \[
   -k(-k^2 + 1) = k^3 - k
   \]

3. Third term:
   \[
   -1(k - 1) = -k + 1
   \]

Putting it all together:

\[
\text{det}(A) = (k + 1) + (k^3 - k) + (-k + 1)
\]

Simplifying this expression:

\[
\text{det}(A) = k + 1 + k^3 - k - k + 1 = k^3 + 2
\]

To find the values of \( k \) for which the determinant is zero, we set:

\[
k^3 + 2 = 0
\]

Solving for \( k \):

\[
k^3 = -2 \implies k = -\sqrt[3]{2}
\]

Thus, the value of \( k \) for which the system has a non-trivial solution is:

\[
\boxed{-\sqrt[3]{2}}
\]
